questions.stem: A study collects data on average total SAT scores and percentage of students who took the exam at 100 randomly selected high schools. The following is part of the computer printout for regression: Variable Coefficient s.e. of coeff t-ratio prob Constant 1176.32 12.65 92.99 ≤ 0.0001 SAT −2.84276 0.2461 −11.55 ≤ 0.0001 R-squared = 76.5% R-squared (adj) = 76.1% Which of the following is a correct conclusion?
questions.answer_text: The negative value of the slope (−2.84276) gives that, on average, the predicted average total SAT score of a school is 2.84 points lower for each one unit higher in the percentage of students taking the exam. Choices (A) through (C) are incorrect for the following reasons. The variable column indicates the independent (explanatory) variable. The sign of the correlation is the same as the sign of the slope (negative here). In this example, the y-intercept is meaningless (predicted SAT result if no students take the exam). There can be a strong linear relation with high r2-value but still a distinct pattern in the residual plot indicating that a nonlinear fit may be even stronger.

questions.stem: Suppose the correlation is negative. Given two points from the scatterplot, which of the following is possible? I. The first point has a larger x-value and a smaller y-value than the second point. II. The first point has a larger x-value and a larger y-value than the second point. III. The first point has a smaller x-value and a larger y-value than the second point.
questions.answer_text: A negative correlation shows a tendency for higher values of one variable to be associated with lower values of the other; however, given any two points, anything is possible.

questions.stem: Suppose the regression line for a set of data, a + 3x, passes through the point (2, 5). If x̅ and y̅ are the sample means of the x- and y-values, respectively, then y̅ =
questions.answer_text: Since (2, 5) is on the line y = a + 3x, we have 5 = a + 3(2) and a = −1. Thus, the regression line is y = −1 + 3x. The point (̅x, y̅ ) is always on the regression line, and so we have y̅ = −1 + 3x̅ .

options.A: A correlation of 0.2 means that 20% of the points are highly correlated.
options.B: Perfect correlation, that is, when the points lie exactly on a straight line, results in r = 0.
options.C: Correlation is not affected by which variable is called x and which is called y.
options.D: A correlation of 0.75 indicates a relationship that is 3 times as linear as one for which the correlation is only 0.25.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about correlation r is true?
questions.answer_text: If the points lie on a straight line, r = ±1. Correlation has the formula , so x and y are interchangeable, and r does not depend on which variable is called x or y. However, since means and standard deviations can be strongly influenced by outliers, r too can be strongly affected by extreme values. Although r = 0.75 indicates a better fit with a linear model than r = 0.25 does, we cannot say that the linearity is threefold.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about residuals from the least squares line are true? I. Residuals may be positive, negative, or zero. II. The linear regression line maximizes the sum of the squares of the residuals. III. A definite pattern in the residual plot is an indication that a nonlinear model will show a better fit to the data than the straight regression line.
questions.answer_text: Residuals can be any sign. In a good straight line fit, the residuals show a random pattern. The linear regression line minimizes, not maximizes, the sum of the squares of the residuals.

questions.stem: In a study of winning percentage in home games versus average home attendance for professional baseball teams, the resulting regression line is Predicted winning percentage = 44 + 0.0003(Attendance) What is the residual if a team has a winning percentage of 55% with an average attendance of 34,000?
questions.answer_text: Predicted winning percentage = 44 + 0.0003(34,000) = 54.2, and Residual = Observed − Predicted = 55 − 54.2 = 0.8.

questions.stem: Suppose the correlation between two variables is −0.57. If each of the y-scores is multiplied by −1, which of the following is true about the new scatterplot?
questions.answer_text: The slope and the correlation coefficient have the same sign. Multiplying every y-value by −1 changes this sign.

options.A: The points in the scatterplot line up in a straight line.
options.B: There is no distinct pattern in the residual plot.

options.D: Each increase of 1,000 square feet in home size gives an increase of 214.1($1,000) in selling price.

questions.stem: A study of selling prices of homes in a southern California community (in $1,000) versus size of the homes (in 1,000s of square feet) shows a moderate positive linear association. The least squares regression equation is Predicted selling price = 35.3 + 214.1(Size). What does “linear” mean in this context?
questions.answer_text: A linear association means that as the explanatory variable (home size here) changes by a constant amount, the response variable (selling price here) also changes by a constant amount, on average. Unless there was perfect linear correlation, the points will not line up on a straight line. No distinct pattern in the residual plot simply means that there is not an obviously better model to be found, but it does not necessarily suggest that the data are linear. The coefficient of determination indicates something about the strength of the relationship but does not define linearity. Choice (D) is an interpretation of the slope, but again, not a definition of linearity.

options.A: The actual incidence of skin cancer at a given latitude will be very close to what is predicted by a least squares model.
options.B: More sun exposure is associated with greater numbers of skin cancer deaths.
options.C: A locale’s incidence of skin cancer deaths has a linear association with its latitude.
options.D: A least squares model predicts that the greater the latitude, the lower the average incidence of skin cancer.

questions.stem: Does lower sun exposure, as measured by greater distance from the equator, result in lower incidence of skin cancer? A study of skin cancer mortality versus latitude of 100 Northern Hemisphere locales shows a strong negative linear association. What does “strong” mean in this context?
questions.answer_text: “Strong” means that the points in the related scatterplot fall close to the least squares regression line. In context, this means that the actual incidence of skin cancer at a given latitude will be very close to what is predicted by the least squares model. Association does not imply causation. Although (C) refers to the existence of an association, and (B) and (D) further refer to the direction of the association, none of these statements refer to the strength of the association.

questions.stem: With regard to a least squares regression line, the sum of the residuals is always zero. Does it follow that the mean or the median of the residuals also must be zero?
questions.answer_text: The mean equals the sum divided by the number of values; thus, if the sum is zero, so is the mean. However, if the sum of values equals zero, it does not follow that the middle value is zero.

questions.stem: The following scatterplot shows the grades for research papers for a sociology professor’s class plotted against the lengths of the papers (in pages). Mary turned in her paper late and was told by the professor that her grade would have been higher if she had turned it in on time. A computer printout fitting a straight line to the data (not including Mary’s score) by the method of least squares gives: (a) Find the correlation coefficient for the relationship between grade and length of paper based on these data (excluding Mary’s paper). (b) What is the slope of the regression line and what does it signify? (c) How will the correlation coefficient change if Mary’s paper is included? Explain your answer. (d) How will the slope of the regression line change if Mary’s paper is included? Explain your answer. (e) Interpret the coefficient of determination in context.
questions.answer_text: (a) The correlation coefficient is . It is positive because the slope of the regression line is positive. (b) The slope is 1.106, signifying that each additional page raises a grade by 1.106, on average. (c) Including Mary’s paper will lower the correlation coefficient because her result seems far off the regression line through the other points. (d) Including Mary’s paper will swing the regression line down and lower the value of the slope. (e) 74.6% of the variation in grades is accounted for by the linear model between grades and page lengths.

questions.stem: A scatterplot of the number of accidents per day on a particular interstate highway during a 30-day month is as follows: (a) Draw a histogram of the frequencies of the number of accidents. (b) Name a feature apparent in the scatterplot but not in the histogram. (c) Name a feature clearly shown by the histogram but not as obvious in the scatterplot.
questions.answer_text: (a) (b) There is a roughly linear trend with daily accidents increasing during the month. (c) The daily number of accidents is strongly skewed to the right.

questions.stem: In a study of how exam scores are influenced by hours of sleep the night before the exam, a random sample of 13 students was outfitted with wristbands that tracked sleep time. The scatterplot of the resulting data follows. (a) Describe the association between exam score and hours of sleep for these 13 students. (b) Describe the association between exam score and hours of sleep for the 8 students who received at least 6 hours of sleep the night before the exam. (c) Explain how the appropriateness of using linear regression is critically influenced by one student’s data.
questions.answer_text: (a) The association between exam score and hours of sleep is nonlinear (or curved), weak (or moderate), and positive. (b) There appears to be very little, if any, association between exam score and hours of sleep for the 8 students who received at least 6 hours of sleep the night before the exam. (Because of the one very low score that also corresponds to hours of sleep just over 6, one could say that there is a very weak positive association.) (c) The student who scored 75 and slept for just over 2 hours the night before the exam has such a strong influence that that particular scatterplot point taken together with all the other points suggests a nonlinear form.

questions.stem: Researchers studying the association between developing dementia and consumption of ultra-processed foods collected data on people 55 years of age or older who showed no signs of dementia at the beginning of the study. Participants filled out questionnaires about daily diet from which the researchers determined how much ultra-processed food was consumed daily on average. The participants were followed for 10 years at which time they were again evaluated for signs of dementia (on a 10-point scale). A scatterplot dementia score on the 10-point scale versus daily ultra-processed food consumed in grams revealed an association described as strong, linear, and positive. (a) Was this an experiment or an observational study? Explain. (b) For the situation described above, explain what is meant by each of the following: i. Strong ii. Linear iii. Positive (c) Is it reasonable to conclude that consumption of ultra-processed foods is one cause of dementia? Explain. (d) What would a positive residual mean in this context?
questions.answer_text: (a) This was an observational study as no treatments were applied. Participants were not instructed to consume quantities of ultra-processed foods. (b) i. A strong relationship means that the data points fell close to a line or curve. ii. A linear relationship means that as consumption of ultra-processed foods increases by 1 gram, the dementia score tends to change by a constant amount on average. iii. A positive relationship means that adults 55 years of age or older who consume more ultra- processed foods tend to have a higher dementia score in 10 years. (c) No, it is not reasonable to conclude causation. Causation cannot be concluded from observational studies, and linear regression can indicate association but not causation. (d) A positive residual would indicate that the linear model underestimated the dementia score for that adult.
